recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If future work wants profile-level ConceptMap publication requirements, follow the CRMI/THO maintenance path identified by FHIR-37959 rather than reintroducing removed profile definitions to core.
issue_request: FHIR-17591 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core, applied for R5, and requested support for publishing ConceptMap artifacts directly in the core specification in the same manner as CodeSystem, ValueSet, and other terminology artifacts.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-17591 was found. Current source shows the request was nevertheless applied: ConceptMap is an active resource in source/fhir.ini, has ConceptMap-specific IG template handling, has source ConceptMap examples including metadata examples, has search parameters, and has a terminology concept maps page using the conceptmapslist macro. R5 follow-on work in J#36190/FHIR-36190 made ConceptMap a MetadataResource and added publication lifecycle metadata support.
additional_context: R5-era source also gained shareableconceptmap and publishableconceptmap profiles, but FHIR-37959 later made a final R6 decision to remove the shareable/publishable/computable/executable profile family from core and maintain those profiles through CRMI/THO. That later applied decision means the current absence of those profile source files should not be treated as a regression for FHIR-17591.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because current build-scoped source already contains direct ConceptMap publication wiring, and restoring removed profile definitions would conflict with FHIR-37959.

related_jiras.note: Published R5 Vocab decision made ConceptMap a MetadataResource and added lifecycle metadata/search parameter support, reinforcing direct publication support.
Applied R6 decision intentionally removed shareable/publishable profile definitions from core and moved ongoing profile maintenance outside core.
